title: The decoder still recurses on the native stack, and a debug build runs out of it before [`DEPTH_CEILING`].
text: [`read`] is a `serde` visitor, one Rust frame per nesting level, and nothing compares the stack it has left with [`nvs_runtime::Ctx::stack_bounds`]. A release build decodes a document at the ceiling even from a task already at its stack's soft limit; a debug build overflows the task's `nvs_host::TASK_STACK_SIZE` at about 800 levels and takes the process down. `a_document_at_the_ceiling_decodes` does not see it, because a test thread's stack is twice a task's. The encoder's heap stack is the shape a fix takes; a check against the armed floor that throws is the smaller one.
